summary: Costa Rica grants visa-free stays of up to 180 days to citizens of the US, Canada, the UK, the EU, Australia, Japan and the other first-group countries of its visa directives, requires a return or onward ticket and at least USD 100 per month of stay, and lets visa-required nationals enter with a valid multiple-entry US, Canadian or Schengen visa, or a US, Canadian, UK or EU residence, instead of a Costa Rican consular visa.

method.text: En el tercer grupo se ubicarán los países cuyos nacionales requerirán visa consular, la cual se entenderá como la autorización que emite un funcionario consular costarricense para ingresar a Costa Rica.

passportValidity.text: Depends on nationality. First-group nationalities (including the US, Canada, the UK, the EU, Australia and Japan) need a passport valid on the day of entry, but you will not be given more days than the passport has left. Second-group nationalities need 90 days' validity, and nationalities that need a visa need 180 days.

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.text: A yellow fever vaccination certificate (ICVP) is required if you are arriving from a country on Costa Rica's risk list: Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, French Guiana, Guyana, Paraguay, Peru, Suriname, Trinidad and Tobago and Venezuela in the Americas, and African countries including Angola, Ethiopia, Ghana, Kenya, Nigeria, Rwanda, Tanzania, Uganda and Zambia. The vaccine must be given at least 10 days before entry.

travelInsurance.text: No official source we could read states a travel insurance requirement for entering Costa Rica. The entry requirements listed in Costa Rica's visa directives (a valid passport, a visa where required, proof of economic means, a return or onward ticket, and no entry ban) do not include it.

notes: When leaving by air you may need to pay a departure tax of USD 29; the UK government says most airlines include it in the ticket price, and if you have to pay it you can use cash or card.

payments.text: Australia's Smartraveller says credit cards are widely accepted and most international hotels and tourist facilities take credit and debit cards, but advises carrying cash for rural areas. Canada's travel advice adds that US dollars are easier to exchange than Canadian dollars and that cash withdrawals need a 4-digit PIN.

safety.text: The UK Foreign Office says muggings and theft are significant problems, particularly on the Atlantic coast, and advises watching your valuables on the beach and not leaving luggage in a parked car, either in view or in the boot. It adds that gang-related violence, including shootings, has become more frequent in urban areas, and that rip currents are very common and there are often no lifeguards.

tips.text: Costa Rica's entry requirements include a return ticket to your country of origin or an onward ticket, and proof of at least USD 100 for each month of your stay.

Australia's Smartraveller says criminals target stationary cars and rental vehicles for robberies, and the UK Foreign Office advises against leaving luggage in a parked car, either in view or in the boot.

The UK government says rip currents are very common on Costa Rica's beaches, there are often no lifeguards, and drownings are the second most common cause of accidental death. It advises seeking reliable local advice.
Australia's Smartraveller advises drinking boiled or bottled water in Costa Rica.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Costa Rica?
faq.answer: No. US citizens are in the first group of Costa Rica's visa directives: visa-free for up to 180 days, with the border officer deciding the days granted. Your passport must be valid on the day of entry (you will not be given more days than it has left), and you need a return or onward ticket and at least USD 100 for each month of your stay.

faq.question: How long can tourists stay in Costa Rica?
faq.answer: Visa-free nationals of the first group (US, Canada, UK, EU, Japan and many more) can be granted up to 180 days; second-group nationals up to 30 days, extendable to 90. The immigration officer decides the exact number of days at entry.

faq.question: Can I enter Costa Rica with a US or Schengen visa instead of a Costa Rican visa?
faq.answer: Yes, if you hold one of the documents Costa Rica's visa directives accept: a valid multiple-entry US or Canadian visa (not a C1, C2 or C3 transit visa) or US or Canadian residence, a multiple-entry Schengen C or D visa, or a residence permit from the UK, the EU, Iceland, Norway or Switzerland that allows multiple entries or is valid for at least 90 more days. With a US, Canadian or Schengen visa or a US or Canadian residence, your stay cannot run beyond its expiry.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever vaccination for Costa Rica?
faq.answer: Only if you are arriving from a country on Costa Rica's yellow fever risk list: Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, French Guiana, Guyana, Paraguay, Peru, Suriname, Trinidad and Tobago, Venezuela, and African countries on the same list. In that case you must show an ICVP certificate for a vaccine given at least 10 days before entry.

faq.question: Do I have to pay a departure tax when leaving Costa Rica?
faq.answer: The UK government says that when leaving by air you may need to pay a departure tax of USD 29, that most airlines include it in the ticket price, and that if you have to pay it you can use cash or card. No official source we could read states the tax for leaving overland.
